clips.instruction: For each question, choose the correct answer. You will hear an interview with a man who moved from the city to a farm.
clips.title: Interview · From city to farm
clips.transcript:
Interviewer: Today I'm talking to Daniel Price, who left his job in the city two years ago to run a small farm. Daniel, why did you decide to change your life?
Daniel: Well, people often think I hated my job, but actually I enjoyed it. The problem was the hours. I was in the office until nine most nights, and I hardly ever saw my children awake. So when my uncle offered to sell me his farm, it felt like the right moment.
Interviewer: Was it difficult at first?
Daniel: Very! I knew nothing about animals. In our first winter, two of our sheep got sick and I had no idea what to do. Luckily, the people on the farms near us were really kind. They taught me almost everything I know.
Interviewer: And what about money?
Daniel: We earn less than before, that's true. But we spend a lot less too. We grow most of our own food, and we don't need two cars any more.
Interviewer: What advice would you give people who want to do the same thing?
Daniel: Don't just dream about it. Try it first. Spend a few weeks working on a farm before you buy one. Some people discover it isn't for them, and that's fine.

questions.prompt: Why did Daniel leave his job in the city?
options: His uncle needed help on the farm.
He had to work very long hours.

questions.prompt: In his first winter on the farm, Daniel…
options: got a lot of help from his neighbours.

questions.prompt: What does Daniel say about money?
options: His family has more money now.
They spend much less than before.
They had to sell both of their cars.

questions.prompt: What is Daniel's advice?
options: Try working on a farm before you decide.
Buy a farm as soon as you can.

passages.instruction: Read the article about a young woman who works abroad. For each question, choose the correct answer.
passages.title: A new start in Auckland
passages.body:
Thu Ha is 25 and comes from Can Tho. Last year, she moved to Auckland, New Zealand, to work in a hotel restaurant.

"I studied English at school, but when I arrived, I couldn't understand people very well," she says. "Everyone spoke so fast! In my first week, a customer asked for a 'flat white' and I brought him a glass of milk. Now I know it's a kind of coffee!"

Thu Ha works five days a week, usually in the evening. On her days off, she goes to English classes at a community centre near her flat. "The classes are free, and I've made friends from Brazil, Korea and Germany there. We always speak English together because it's the only language we all know."

The hardest thing for Thu Ha is the weather. "In Can Tho it's hot all year. Here, the winter is cold and wet, and I had to buy my first real coat." But she loves her new life. "Next year I want to study hotel management. My manager has offered to help me find a good course."

questions.prompt: When Thu Ha first arrived in Auckland,
options: she found it hard to understand people.

questions.prompt: What happened with the customer in her first week?
options: She gave him the wrong drink.

questions.prompt: Why does Thu Ha speak English with her classmates?
options: They want to pass an exam.
They have no other language in common.

questions.prompt: What does Thu Ha say about the weather in Auckland?
options: It is similar to the weather in Can Tho.
She needed to buy warm clothes for it.
The summer is too hot for her.

questions.prompt: What are Thu Ha's plans for the future?
options: Her manager will help her start studying.
She wants to go back to Can Tho.
She hopes to become a manager next year.

parts.title: Writing
parts.promptBody:
You have just moved to a new city. Write an email to your English-speaking friend (50–80 words). Tell your friend:

  1. where you live now and who you live with
  2. what you usually do at weekends
  3. whether you like your new home, and why / why not
